chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ الْكَرِيمِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو بْنِ صَالِحٍ، الْخَثْعَمِيُّ، مَوْلَاهُمْ، كُوفِيٌّ، يُلَقَّبُ "كَرَّامًا". الْوَاقِفَةُ تَدْعِيهِ، وَالْغُلَاةُ تَرْوِي عَنْهُ كَثِيرًا.

translations.en: Abd al-Karim ibn Amr ibn Salih, al-Khath'ami, their client, Kufan, was nicknamed "Karram". The Waqifa claim him, and the Ghulat narrate much from him.

en.summary: This entry highlights Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, a Kufan narrator whose theological alignment was contested between the Waqifa, who claimed him for their doctrine of halting at the Imams, and the Ghulat, who drew heavily from his narrations. His dual association illustrates the complex sectarian landscape of early Kufa, where boundaries between moderate sects and extremists were often blurred in biographical records.
en.seo_question: Who is Abd al-Karim al-Karram and which Shia sects claim him?

key_terms.الوَاقِفَةُ: The Waqifa, a Shia sect that believed the Imam stopped at Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْغُلَاةُ: The Ghulat, Shia extremists who attributed divine qualities to the Imams
key_terms.يُلَقَّبُ: He was nicknamed/called by the laqab
key_terms.كَرَّامًا: Karram, the nickname of the narrator
